cues.zh: 欢迎我们的演讲者，Robert Wills。
cues.en: I'd like to welcome our speaker, uh Robert Wills.

cues.zh: 他是 Cisco 在 Harpenden 的工程师，为互联网路由器编写软件。
cues.en: He's an engineer at uh Cisco in Harpenden, and uh he writes software for uh internet routers.

cues.zh: 他对计算的历史、用户以及他们实际用计算机做了什么很感兴趣。
cues.en: Um he's a keen interest in the history of computing and users and what they actually did with the computers.

cues.zh: 过去 10 年里，他一直着迷于 Apollo 制导计算机，而且仍在不断了解它。
cues.en: And uh has been fascinated by the Apollo guidance computer for the last 10 years and is still learning things about it.

cues.zh: 今天他要讲的是 50 年前 7 月登月下降的最后阶段。
cues.en: Uh today he's going to tell us about the final stages of the uh lunar descent, uh which was 50 years ago, uh in July.

cues.zh: 以及那令人揪心的三秒钟，当时任务看起来不得不中止。
cues.en: Um and uh the three nail biting seconds in which it appeared that the mission would have to be aborted.

cues.zh: 那么废话不多说，有请 Robert Wills。
cues.en: So without further ado, Robert Wills.
July the 20th, 1969.

cues.zh: Neil Armstrong 和 Buzz Aldrin 在登月舱里，位于地表上方 3 万英尺，正在快速下降。
cues.en: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin were in the lunar lander 30,000 feet above the surface and descending rapidly.

cues.zh: 一切似乎都很顺利，突然机载计算机显示 1202 程序报警，随后计算机重启了。
cues.en: All seemed to be going well when suddenly the onboard computer indicated a 1202 program alarm and the computer restarted.

cues.zh: Neil Armstrong 一如既往冷静沉着，通过无线电联系休斯顿，语气中只带一丝急迫，询问那个 1202 报警的最新情况。
cues.en: Neil Armstrong, as ever, remained cool, calm, and collected, and radioed Houston with just a hint of urgency in his voice asking for an update on that 1202 alarm.

cues.zh: 三秒后，休斯顿回复，允许 Armstrong 继续。
cues.en: Three seconds later, Houston came back and gave Armstrong the go to continue.

cues.zh: 不久后，又出现一次程序报警，这次是 1201，接着又一次、又一次、又一次。
cues.en: Shortly after, another program alarm occurred, this time a 1201, and another, and another, and another.

cues.zh: 在 Apollo 11 下降过程中，总共出现了五次程序报警和重启，最后一次距月球表面只有 2000 英尺。
cues.en: In total, during the Apollo 11 descent, there were five program alarms and restarts, the last one just 2,000 feet above the moon's surface.

cues.zh: 飞行过程中，没有比这更糟糕的时机出现计算机故障了。
cues.en: There could not be a worse time in the flight to have computer problems.

cues.zh: 当时，媒体津津乐道地报道：Armstrong 从瘫痪失灵的机载计算机手中夺过手动控制权，英勇地独自一人排除万难，将飞船降落在月球表面。
cues.en: Now at the time, the press gleefully reported how Armstrong seized manual control from a crippled and failing onboard computer and managed to heroically and single handedly land the spaceship on the surface of the moon against all odds.

cues.zh: 事实远非如此。
cues.en: Nothing could be further from the truth.

cues.zh: 是的，Neil Armstrong 是一位杰出而才华横溢的飞行员，但阿波罗导航计算机在这次任务以及它参与的其他所有任务中都运行得完美无误。
cues.en: Yes, Neil Armstrong was an outstanding and brilliant pilot, but the Apollo guidance computer worked flawlessly in this mission and every other mission that it flew.

cues.zh: 这得益于开创性的硬件和软件设计原则，这些原则让系统能够抵御任何故障，无论发生什么。
cues.en: This was thanks to pioneering hardware and software design principles which were used to make the system robust against any failure, no matter what happened.

cues.zh: 这些设计原则虽然当时颇具革命性，如今却构成了我们每天使用的各类高可靠软件的基础。
cues.en: And those design principles, although pretty revolutionary at the time, now form the basis of all sorts of highly reliable software that we use every day.

cues.zh: 所以在这场演讲中，我想借阿波罗11号的故事，给大家讲讲呃阿波罗导航计算机。
cues.en: So in this presentation, I'd like to use the story of Apollo 11 to tell you a bit about the uh Apollo guidance computer.

cues.zh: 我先呃实际介绍一下这台计算机，然后详细带大家了解如何登月，并展示这台计算机以及它在呃登月过程中扮演的角色。
cues.en: So I'll start by uh actually introducing the computer to you and then I'll walk you through in detail how you land on the moon and I'll show you the computer and the role that it played in uh doing the landing.

cues.zh: 接下来，我会讲讲我们用来让软件保持健壮的一些革命性设计原则。
cues.en: Next, I'll talk about some of those revolutionary design principles that we used to make the software robust.

cues.zh: 最后，等这些背景都讲完，我会再回顾阿波罗11号登月，弄清那些程序报警到底是怎么回事。
cues.en: And then finally, once we've got all that background, I'll go back over the Apollo 11 landing and we'll get to the bottom of those program alarms.

cues.zh: 我会向你们证明，是阿波罗制导计算机拯救了这次任务，而不是毁了它。
cues.en: And I will show you that the Apollo guidance computer saved the mission rather than ruining it.

cues.zh: 不过首先，简单说说我自己。正如介绍中提到的，过去10年我一直在思科的服务提供商业务部门工作。
cues.en: First though, a little bit about me, so as uh was said in the introduction, I've been working at Cisco for the last 10 years in the service provider business unit.

cues.zh: 我们为那种平时根本见不到的顶级路由器编写软件。
cues.en: So we uh we write software for really top of the range routers that you wouldn't normally see.

cues.zh: 这些路由器位于数据中心乃至整个国家网络的核心，所以它们必须非常可靠，这一点至关重要。
cues.en: These things sit in the core of like a data center or a whole country's network and so it's really important that these routers are very reliable.

cues.zh: 所以，我工作中做的很多事情，和我今天要讲的一些主题之间有很多联系。
cues.en: And so there's a lot of links between the things that I do as part of my job and some of the topics that I'm going to be talking about today.

cues.zh: 业余时间，我特别痴迷计算技术史，而且我认为老计算机不该被摆在架子上积灰。
cues.en: In my spare time, I absolutely love the history of computing and I believe that old computers should not sit on a shelf and gather dust.

cues.zh: 它们应该被插上电、开机、重新焕发生机，并在它们原本设计的应用场景中演示出来。
cues.en: But they should be plugged in, switched on, brought to life and demonstrated in the context with which they were designed to be used.

cues.zh: 或者，如果你手边没有阿波罗导航计算机和飞船，至少试着在屏幕上演示一下。
cues.en: Or, if you don't have an Apollo guidance computer and a spaceship handy, at least try and demonstrate it on the screen.

cues.zh: 我花了 10 年时间研究阿波罗导航计算机，它是我最喜欢的一台机器，原因有很多，尤其是今天我就要讲的那个故事。
cues.en: And I spent 10 years researching the Apollo guidance computer, it's my favorite for all sorts of reasons, not least the story I'm going to tell you today.

cues.zh: 好，首先让我来介绍这台了不起的机器。
cues.en: Okay, so first let me introduce you to this amazing machine.

cues.zh: 所以它就在屏幕上。
cues.en: So there it is on the screen.

cues.zh: 它是在 MIT 仪器实验室设计的。
cues.en: And it was designed at the MIT instrumentation laboratory.

cues.zh: 它其实是 NASA 在阿波罗计划中授予的第一份合同。
cues.en: It was actually the first contract that NASA awarded as part of the Apollo program.

cues.zh: 阿波罗计划启动仅 6 周，NASA 就授予了这份合同，他们意识到需要某种机载计算机。
cues.en: So just 6 weeks into the Apollo program starting, NASA awarded this contract and they realized that some sort of onboard computer would be needed.

cues.zh: 它负责阿波罗任务几乎所有的制导、导航和控制。
cues.en: And it was responsible for almost all of the guidance, navigation and control of the Apollo missions.

cues.zh: 它成功把你送入地球轨道，又把你带到月球。
cues.en: So it managed, it got got you into orbit around the earth, it got you to the moon.

cues.zh: 它把你送入月球轨道。
cues.en: It got you into orbit around the moon.

cues.zh: 它把你送到月球表面。
cues.en: It got you down onto the surface.

cues.zh: 它又把你从月面带回。
cues.en: It got you back off again.

cues.zh: 它成功让两艘飞船重新交会。
cues.en: It managed to rendezvous the two ships back together.

cues.zh: 它把这一整套都带回地球，并完成了再入。
cues.en: It got the whole kaboodle back to earth and it managed reentry.

cues.zh: 同样的硬件，但运行不同的软件，它同时用在指令舱——也就是母船——和登月舱上，后者才是真正登上月球的那个。
cues.en: The same hardware, but running different software, was used in both the command module, so that's the mothership, and the lunar module, that's the thing that landed on the moon.

cues.zh: 它只有 32 公斤重。
cues.en: It weighed only 32 kg.

cues.zh: 这一点非常关键，因为这份重量你要付三次代价。
cues.en: This is really important because you pay for the weight three times.

cues.zh: 你要花钱把它送出地球，花钱让它降落到月球，还要再花钱把它从月球带回来。
cues.en: You pay to get it off the earth, you pay to land it on the moon and you pay to get it off again.

cues.zh: 它只消耗 55 瓦，每次我讲这个内容，都要再核对一遍这个数字，因为我实在难以相信。
cues.en: It consumed only 55 watts and every time I give this presentation, I double check that number because I just don't believe it.

cues.zh: 它只占 1 立方英尺。
cues.en: And it occupied only 1 cubic foot.

cues.zh: 要知道，在那个年代，大多数计算机要占满整个房间，耗电巨大，还需要大量制冷。
cues.en: Now, in an era where most computers occupied entire rooms, consumed vast amounts of power and required huge amounts of cooling.

cues.zh: 我觉得这三个数字真的很了不起。
cues.en: I think those three numbers are truly remarkable.

cues.zh: 它的运行速度是每秒 5 万到 10 万条指令。
cues.en: And it ran at between 50 and 100,000 instructions per second.

cues.zh: 这就是“你口袋里的计算器比阿波罗制导计算机还强”这个说法的来源。
cues.en: This is where the claim comes from that there's more power in your pocket calculator than the Apollo guidance computer.

cues.zh: 而你就会看到，这完全是一派胡言。
cues.en: That, as you will see, is a load of rubbish.

cues.zh: 现在再讲得技术一点，它完全是从零开始造的。
cues.en: So getting a little bit more techie now, it was built completely from scratch.

cues.zh: 只用一种逻辑门：三输入或非门。
cues.en: From one type of logic gate, the three input NOR gate.

cues.zh: 这是你能想到的最简单的逻辑门。
cues.en: So this is the simplest possible logic gate you could ever think of.

cues.zh: 他们把这些逻辑门连了大约 5500 个，结果发现，把它们连起来就能构成你能想到的任何数字电路。
cues.en: And they were able to connect about 5 and a half thousand of these logic gates together and it turns out that you can connect them together to make any digital circuit you can think of.

cues.zh: 它实际上是用集成电路造的，每个集成电路上有两个这种逻辑门。
cues.en: Now it was it was actually built from integrated circuits and so you had uh two of those uh logic gates on each integrated circuit.

cues.zh: 因此这台计算机由略少于 3000 个集成电路组成。
cues.en: And so the computer was made up of just under 3,000 integrated circuits.

cues.zh: 现在看，选用集成电路这个决定本身就非常超前。
cues.en: Now, the choice to use integrated circuits was itself really ahead of its time.

cues.zh: 比如 1963 年，全美国集成电路总产量的 60% 都给了 MIT，用于阿波罗制导计算机。
cues.en: For example, in 1963, 60% of the United States entire integrated circuit production went to MIT for the Apollo guidance computer.

cues.zh: 所以你看，他们用集成电路这件事有多激进。
cues.en: So that's how radical it was that they were using integrated circuits.

cues.zh: 他们是用锡焊把它们焊在一起的吗？并不是。
cues.en: Did they solder them together? Oh no.

cues.zh: 而是焊接在一起，组成这些模块。
cues.en: They welded them together to form these modules.

cues.zh: 然后 26 个模块插到一块背板上，背板把所有模块连接起来，组成最终的计算机。
cues.en: And then 26 modules plugged in to a backplane and the backplane connected all the modules together and made the final computer.

cues.zh: 这里有一张稍大一点的照片，是托盘，上面插着一些模块。
cues.en: There's a slightly bigger picture of the tray with some modules um plugged into it.

cues.zh: 还有一张另一侧的照片，那就是背板。
cues.en: And there's a picture of the other side, that's the backplane.

cues.zh: 你能看到那些蓝线，其实是一些细导线，把所有模块连接在一起。
cues.en: Those blue lines you can see a little wires that are connecting all the modules together.

cues.zh: 内存方面，那台计算机的内存真的非常非常少。
cues.en: In terms of memory, there was a really, really tiny amount of memory in the computer.

cues.zh: 所以它有 2000 个字的可擦除内存，也就是我们说的 RAM，变量就存在那里。
cues.en: So there were 2,000 words of erasable memory, what we would call RAM, and that's where variables would be stored.

cues.zh: 用大白话说，就是你的计算机里能存 2000 个不同的数字。
cues.en: So in English, that means you can store 2,000 different numbers in your computer.

cues.zh: 比如，你可能存当前位置，也可能存将要着陆的位置，还可能存速度之类的各种其他信息。
cues.en: For example, you might store where you are, you might store where you're going to be landing, you might store uh various other bits of information like your speed.

cues.zh: 所以你只能存 2000 个这样的数字，相信我，这真的不多。
cues.en: So you can store just 2,000 of those numbers which, believe me, is not very much.

cues.zh: 它还有 36000 个字的固定内存，也就是我们说的 ROM，程序就存在那里。
cues.en: And it had 36,000 words of fixed memory, what we would call ROM, and that's where the program was stored.

cues.zh: 再用大白话说，就是你的计算机里能存 36000 条指令。
cues.en: And so more in English again, that means you can store 36,000 instructions in your computer.

cues.zh: 所以那两样东西其实都不多。
cues.en: So really not very much of either of those things.

cues.zh: 不过，这个固定存储器还挺酷的。
cues.en: Now, the fixed memory is pretty cool.

cues.zh: 它其实就在这张幻灯片上，你能看到这些非常细的铜线，这里都是放大的。
cues.en: So it's actually here on the slide and you can see there's these very thin copper wires, this is all magnified.

cues.zh: 这些非常细的铜线穿过这些环。
cues.en: These very thin copper wires going through these rings.

cues.zh: 大致来说，一根线穿过环就是 1，没穿过就是 0。
cues.en: And roughly speaking, if a wire went through a ring, that was a one, and if it didn't, that was a zero.

cues.zh: 所以软件真的就是被编织起来，形成了固定存储器。
cues.en: And so the software was literally woven together to form the fixed memory.

cues.zh: 有一张 Raytheon 工程师的照片，她面前就摆着程序清单，正非常小心地把那些微小的铜线穿过更微小的环。
cues.en: There's a picture of an engineer at Raytheon, she effectively has um the program listing in front of her and she is very carefully weaving those tiny copper wires through the even tinier uh rings.

cues.zh: 以此把程序转译进固定存储器，让计算机随后能够读取。
cues.en: To translate the program into the fixed memory that the computer can then read.

cues.zh: 你可不想在那里犯错，对吧？
cues.en: You wouldn't want to make a mistake there, would you?

cues.zh: 那么，考虑到它只由5个半呃逻辑门组成，它的功能丰富得令人意外。
cues.en: Now, given it was made up of only 5 and a half um logic gates, it was surprisingly featureful.

cues.zh: 它有实时时钟、中断、奇偶校验，以及丰富的输入输出连接能力。
cues.en: It had a real time clock, interrupts, parity checking, and extensive input and output connectivity.

cues.zh: 但它也有一些怪癖。
cues.en: But it also had some quirks.

cues.zh: 它的字长是15位。
cues.en: It had a 15 bit word size.

cues.zh: 这意味着，它能存储的数字并不大。
cues.en: What that means is, it the numbers it can store are not very big.

cues.zh: 它的整数用反码表示，这会让任何数学家大受震撼，因为零可以有两种不同的值。
cues.en: It used one's complement for integers, which will shock any mathematician, because you can have two different values for zero.

cues.zh: 正零和负零。
cues.en: Positive zero and minus zero.

cues.zh: 相信我，由于显而易见的原因，今天的任何计算机系统都不用它。
cues.en: And believe me, this is not used in any computer system today for obvious reasons.

cues.zh: 它没有浮点数，所以不能用带小数点的数。
cues.en: It had no floating point numbers, so you couldn't have anything with a decimal point.

cues.zh: 一切都必须是整数，但其实这也没那么糟，你可以应付，而且很多方面这样反而更好。
cues.en: Everything had to be a whole number, but actually, it turns out that's not too bad, you can work with that, and in many ways that's preferable.

cues.zh: 而且嗯，它没有很多不同的指令，而是靠这些奇怪的内存位置做了不少事。
cues.en: And um instead of having lots of different instructions, it did quite a lot with these weird memory locations.

cues.zh: 比如，它没有一条专门把数字左移一位的指令，而在计算机里这其实是非常有用的操作。
cues.en: So for example, rather than a special instruction to shift a number one place to the left, which turns out to be a really useful thing to be able to do in a computer.

cues.zh: 要做这件事，不需要专门指令，而是把数字写到特殊位置 20，然后神奇的是，再读回来时，数字就左移了一位。
cues.en: Rather than a special instruction to do that, you would write your number into the special location 20, and then magically when you read it back again, you get the number shifted one place to the left.

cues.zh: 所以这算是这些指令的另一个怪癖。
cues.en: So that was kind of another quirk of the instructions.

cues.zh: 如我们所见，它的内存非常少，没有栈，指令集也怪异又别扭。
cues.en: As we've seen, it had a very tiny amount of memory, it had no stack and a bizarre and awkward instruction set.

cues.zh: 如果把 Apollo Guidance Computer 的指令交给现代系统工程师，他们肯定会挠头，努力想怎么用这些指令写出程序。
cues.en: If you gave a modern day systems engineer the Apollo guidance computer's instructions, they would be really scratching their heads to try and figure out how to use those instructions to make a program.

cues.zh: 好，我们来聊聊 I/O。
cues.en: Okay, let's talk about IO.

cues.zh: 屏幕上这个东西叫 DSKY，是宇航员与制导计算机交互的主要方式。
cues.en: So, this thing on the screen called the disky, was the main way that the astronauts interacted with the guidance computer.

cues.zh: 可以看到，它右上方有一块显示屏，能显示一些数字。
cues.en: And you can see it's got a display on the top right that can show you some numbers.

cues.zh: 底部有一个小键盘，用来输入一些数据。
cues.en: It's got a keypad at the bottom for entering some data.

cues.zh: 左上方你勉强能看到它有一些特殊的灯。
cues.en: And on the top left, you can just about see it's got some special lights.

cues.zh: DSKY 使用“动词 + 名词”的格式来输入命令和显示数据。
cues.en: The disky used a verb noun format for entering commands and displaying data.

cues.zh: 飞船里还有许多其他的人机接口设备，比如 eight ball、指示灯和手控器。
cues.en: And there were many other human interface devices present in the spaceship, for example, the eight ball, indicator lamps, and hand controllers.

cues.zh: 之后，呃，我会把这些都展示给你们看。
cues.en: And I will show you all of this, um later on.

cues.zh: 这台计算机还能通过无线电把数据传回休斯敦，并从休斯敦接收数据。
cues.en: The computer could also radio data back to Houston and receive data from Houston.

cues.zh: 当然，嗯，飞船有很多非常激动人心的 IO，比如火箭发动机就是 IO。
cues.en: And of course, um a spaceship has lots of very exciting IO, for example, a rocket engine is IO.

cues.zh: 计算机能够控制火箭发动机。
cues.en: The computer is able to control the rocket engine.

cues.zh: 它还能从许多专用仪器读取数据，这些我后面还会再讲。
cues.en: It's also able to read data from lots of specialized instruments which again I'll talk about later.

cues.zh: 所以，制导计算机特别擅长的一件事——因为它必须擅长——就是输入和输出。
cues.en: So, one of the things that the guidance computer was really good at because it had to be, was input and output.

cues.zh: 好，计算机就说到这，现在我想和大家聊聊阿波罗是如何登月的。
cues.en: Okay, so that's the computer, now I'd like to talk to you a bit about how they landed on the moon with Apollo.

cues.zh: 首先，我们需要一艘飞船。
cues.en: First of all, we're going to need a spaceship.

cues.zh: 这就是我们的飞船。
cues.en: So here's our spaceship.

cues.zh: 我们首先需要一台大型火箭发动机，它能提供很大的推力。
cues.en: And the first thing that we need is a big rocket engine, and that rocket engine will give us lots of thrust.

cues.zh: 我们会用这个推力来减速，让我们脱离轨道，轻轻降落到月面。
cues.en: And we'll use that thrust to slow ourselves down, that will take us out of orbit and gently onto the surface.

cues.zh: 这就是我们的大火箭发动机。
cues.en: So there's our big rocket engine.

cues.zh: 不过，我们还得能转向，这就是这些小 RCS 推进器的工作。
cues.en: However, we also need to be able to steer, and that's the job of these little RCS thrusters.

cues.zh: RCS 推进器让计算机能把航天器转向任何方向。
cues.en: The RCS thrusters allow the computer to steer the spacecraft in any direction.

cues.zh: 主要的数据来源是这个叫 IMU 的东西。
cues.en: The main source of data is this thing called the IMU.

cues.zh: IMU 能告诉你航天器正朝向哪个方向。
cues.en: The IMU can tell you which way the spacecraft is pointing.

cues.zh: 它还能告诉你航天器正在往哪个方向加速。
cues.en: And it can tell you which way the spacecraft is accelerating.

cues.zh: 有了这些信息，你就能算出位置和速度。
cues.en: And with those bits of information, you can calculate the position and the speed.

cues.zh: 还有着陆雷达，它用雷达测量飞船距离月球表面的高度。
cues.en: There's also the landing radar which uses radar to measure the height of the spaceship above the moon's surface.

cues.zh: 这是窗户。
cues.en: There's the window.

cues.zh: 这扇窗非常重要，之后我会详细讲讲。
cues.en: The window is very important, I'll have a lot to say about that later.

cues.zh: 航天器的支脚上装有一些小探针，叫作月球接触探针。
cues.en: On the feet of the spacecraft are these little probes called the lunar contact probes.

cues.zh: 中间把这一切串起来的，是我们的好朋友——Apollo 制导计算机。
cues.en: And in the middle, tying everything together, sits our best friend, the Apollo guidance computer.

cues.zh: 这就是我们的飞船。
cues.en: So that's our spaceship.

cues.zh: 我快速讲几件你们可能不太熟悉的东西。
cues.en: I'll just talk very quickly about a couple of things that will be less familiar to you.

cues.zh: 首先是 RCS 推进器。
cues.en: First, the RCS thrusters.

cues.zh: 飞船的四个角上各有一组四联 RCS 推进器，一个朝上，一个朝下，还有两个朝外、成直角。
cues.en: So on four corners of the spacecraft are these quads of RCS thrusters, one pointing up, one pointing down and two pointing out at right angles.

cues.zh: 计算机可以让这些微型推进器喷出小股推力。
cues.en: And the computer can give little squirts of thrust through these tiny thrusters.

cues.zh: 利用这些小股推力，它就能按计算机想要的方向操纵飞船。
cues.en: And uh using those little squirts, it can steer the spacecraft in any direction the computer wants to.

cues.zh: 另一件值得快速一提的是 IMU。
cues.en: The other thing worth talking about quickly is the IMU.

cues.zh: IMU 是一件了不起的工程作品。
cues.en: The IMU was a remarkable piece of engineering.

cues.zh: 它是一个球体，球体内部有三个——抱歉，是两个同心环，它们可以彼此相对旋转。
cues.en: It was a sphere and inside the sphere were two uh three, sorry, concentric rings which could rotate around each other.

cues.zh: 然后，在 IMU 正中间有一个叫稳定部件的东西。
cues.en: And then right in the middle of the IMU was something called the stable member.

cues.zh: 稳定部件上装有三个陀螺仪，彼此成直角安装。
cues.en: The stable member had three gyroscopes on it, mounted at right angles to each other.

cues.zh: 呃，因为它们是陀螺仪，所以能让稳定部件在空间中完全保持固定。
cues.en: And uh because they were gyroscopes, that keeps the stable member completely fixed in space.

cues.zh: 所以航天器可以随意移动，而稳定部件始终完全停在原位。
cues.en: So the spacecraft can move around however it likes and the stable member stays completely in the same place.

cues.zh: 现在，同心环上装有传感器，你可以用这些传感器测出航天器相对稳定部件是如何转动的，而稳定部件始终固定不动。
cues.en: Now, there are sensors on the concentric rings and you can use those sensors to see how the spacecraft has turned around the stable member, which is always fixed.

cues.zh: 因此，通过这些测量，你就能测出航天器指向哪个方向。
cues.en: And so by taking those measurements, you can measure which way the spacecraft is pointing.

cues.zh: 另外还有三个加速度计，有点像你手机里的那种，可以测量三个方向上的加速度。
cues.en: And there are also three accelerometers, a bit like in your phone, that can measure the acceleration in three directions.

cues.zh: 好，关于飞船就讲这么多，知道这些就够了。
cues.en: Okay, so that's enough about the spaceship, that's all you need to know about that.

cues.zh: 接下来，我得给你们上一堂两分钟的速成课，把 NASA 几百小时的训练浓缩成两分钟。
cues.en: Next, I need to give you a two minutes uh course, I need to condense hundreds of hours of NASA training into two minutes.

cues.zh: 再讲讲他们是怎么用 Apollo 登上月球的。
cues.en: And tell you uh how they landed on the moon with Apollo.

cues.zh: 我先给你们交代一下背景。
cues.en: So let me set the scene for you.

cues.zh: 我们进入任务时，宇航员正处于所谓的下降轨道。
cues.en: We're coming into the mission at the point where the astronauts are in what was called the descent orbit.

cues.zh: 这个名字其实很误导，因为下降轨道并不会真的把你带到月球表面。
cues.en: Now this is a really misleading name, because the descent orbit doesn't actually take you down to the surface of the moon.

cues.zh: 下降轨道是一个椭圆，最低点在月面上方 9 海里。
cues.en: The descent orbit is an ellipse, and the lowest point of the descent orbit is 9 nautical miles above the surface.

cues.zh: 登月舱完全可以沿着这条下降轨道一圈又一圈地永远飞下去。
cues.en: And the lunar module could quite happily go around and around that descent orbit forever and ever.

cues.zh: 为了登月，我们需要从轨道最低点开始执行一系列机动。
cues.en: In order to land on the moon, we need to execute a series of maneuvers starting from that lowest point in the orbit.

cues.zh: 这些机动会带我们离开轨道，缓缓降落到月面。
cues.en: And those maneuvers will take us out of orbit and gently down onto the surface.

cues.zh: 这些机动是着陆中最难的部分，也是我今天要讲的内容。
cues.en: Those maneuvers are the hardest bits of the landing, and that's the thing I'm going to be talking about today.

cues.zh: 这个过程分为三个阶段。
cues.en: Now that comes in three phases.

cues.zh: 第一个是 P63，制动阶段。
cues.en: The first is P63, the braking phase.

cues.zh: P63 的目标是让飞船减速。
cues.en: Now the aim of P63 is to slow the spacecraft down.

cues.zh: 飞船减速的同时，也会损失大量高度。
cues.en: And as the spacecraft slows down, it will also lose lots of height.

cues.zh: 飞船开始时位于月面上方 9 海里，也就是 50,000 英尺处，速度非常快，达到每秒 1,670 米。
cues.en: So the spacecraft starts 9 nautical miles or 50,000 feet above the surface and it's going really fast, 1,670 meters per second.

cues.zh: 在 P63 期间，我们点燃那台巨大的火箭发动机，让飞船减速，同时失去大部分高度。
cues.en: During P63, we fire that massive rocket engine, that slows us down, we lose most of our height.

cues.zh: 所以在 P63 结束时，我们低多了，距月面只有 8,000 英尺。
cues.en: So at the end of P63, we're much lower, we're only 8,000 feet above the surface.

cues.zh: 速度也慢多了，每秒 210 米。
cues.en: And we're going much slower, 210 meters per second.

cues.zh: 这就是 P63。
cues.en: So that's P63.

cues.zh: 接下来是 P64，接近阶段。
cues.en: Next is P64, the approach phase.

cues.zh: 到现在为止，大体上说，宇航员一直仰卧着，火箭发动机朝他们前方，他们其实看不清自己要去哪儿。
cues.en: Now, up until this point, the astronauts, broadly speaking, are on their backs with the rocket engine pointing out in front of them, and they can't really see where they're going.

cues.zh: 所以 P64 开始时发生的第一件事，就是俯仰翻转机动。
cues.en: So the first thing that happens at the start of P64 is that pitch over maneuver.

cues.zh: 这让宇航员能透过窗户向前看，看到将要着陆的地点。
cues.en: And that allows the astronauts to see forward out of the window to see where they're going to be landing.

cues.zh: 这还挺有用的。
cues.en: Which is kind of useful.

cues.zh: 在 P64 期间，宇航员和计算机协同工作，微调着陆点。
cues.en: During P64, the astronauts and the computer work together to fine tune the landing site.

cues.zh: 最后，当登月舱离地面约 200 英尺，基本上位于着陆点上方时，我们进入 P66。
cues.en: Finally, when the lunar module is about 200 feet off the ground and it's basically above the landing site, we enter P66.

cues.zh: 最后一个阶段。
cues.en: The final phase.

cues.zh: P66 的目标是平稳、轻柔地垂直着陆，不出现任何左右或前后的移动。
cues.en: The aim of P66 is to touch down nice and gently, vertically, and without any side to side or forwards or backwards movement.

cues.zh: 这就是三个着陆阶段：P63，制动阶段，我们在这里减速并降掉大部分高度。
cues.en: So that's the three landing phases, P63, the braking phase, where we slow down and lose most of our height.

cues.zh: P64，接近阶段，宇航员和计算机协作，微调着陆点。
cues.en: P64, the approach phase, where the astronauts and the computer work together to fine tune the landing site.

cues.zh: 还有 P66，最后阶段，我们要轻柔平稳地着陆。
cues.en: And P66, the final phase, where we want to touch down in a nice and gentle manner.

cues.zh: 好，他们当时就是这么做的。
cues.en: Okay, so that's that's how they did it.

cues.zh: 现在，我想把时间倒回去，让大家看看计算机实际运行、干活的样子。
cues.en: Now, I'd like to rewind the clock and show you the computer in action doing its stuff.

cues.zh: 这里细节挺多的，但你不用记住任何细节，也能享受后面的内容，我只是想给大家演示一下宇航员和计算机当时在做的那些事，让你感受一下到底发生了什么。
cues.en: Now, there's quite a lot of detail here and you don't need to remember any of the detail to enjoy to enjoy the rest of the talk, I just want to uh sort of demonstrate to you the sort of things that the astronauts and the computer were doing, so you get a flavor for what's happening.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 我们把时间倒回去。
cues.en: So let's rewind the clock.

cues.zh: 我们回到了下降轨道，距离计划开始呃着陆机动还有大约 10 分钟。
cues.en: We're back in the descent orbit and we're about 10 minutes before we're due to start the uh landing maneuver.

cues.zh: 宇航员面前是 DSKY，记住这是他们与计算机交互的主要方式。
cues.en: The astronauts have the disky in front of them, remember that's the main way that they interact with the computer.

cues.zh: 他们首先要做的是加载着陆软件。
cues.en: The first thing they need to do is load the landing software.

cues.zh: 为此，他们输入 Verb 37，意思是请加载这个程序，然后输入程序编号。
cues.en: So to do that, they type in verb 37, which means please load this program and then they type in the program number.

cues.zh: 也就是 Program 63。
cues.en: So program 63.

cues.zh: 他们按下回车，计算机便加载着陆软件。
cues.en: They press enter and the computer loads the landing software.

cues.zh: 计算机已经预先编入了着陆点应该在哪里的信息。
cues.en: Now, the computer has been programmed ahead of time with where the landing site should be.

cues.zh: 计算机会算出它需要在什么确切时间开始点燃火箭发动机，以启动那次着陆机动。
cues.en: And the computer calculates at exactly what time it needs to start firing the rocket engine to start that landing maneuver.

cues.zh: 计算机会用 Verb 6 Noun 61 向宇航员显示这条信息，意思是：我有一些关于着陆的信息要给你看。
cues.en: So the computer displays that to the astronauts using verb 6 noun 61, which means I have some information about the landing to show you.

cues.zh: 如果你迫不及待想落到月面，最有趣的数字就是第二个：距离点火还有多久。
cues.en: And the most interesting number, if you're excited about getting to the surface, is the second one, the time until ignition.

cues.zh: 这里显示的是 600 秒，之后计算机认为我们需要，呃，点燃发动机。
cues.en: So, here it's saying it's 600 seconds before the computer's calculated that we need to um light the engine.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 快进一下，现在我们距离点火还有 100 秒。
cues.en: So, fast forward, we're now 100 seconds before ignition.

cues.zh: 计算机有一条重要消息。
cues.en: And the computer has an important message.

cues.zh: 为了向宇航员提示这一点，它会点亮 DSKY 上的 Key Release 灯。
cues.en: So to signal that to the astronauts, it illuminates the key release light on the disky.

cues.zh: 宇航员按下 Key Release 按钮就能查看这条消息。
cues.en: The astronauts can view that message by pressing the key release button.

cues.zh: 这条消息是 Verb 50、Noun 18。
cues.en: And the message is verb 50, noun 18.

cues.zh: 这是什么意思？
cues.en: What does that mean?

cues.zh: 这是计算机在请求允许它操纵飞船。
cues.en: Well, that is the computer asking permission to maneuver the spacecraft.

cues.zh: 还记得吗，P63 开始时，我们需要让飞船差不多仰躺着，火箭发动机朝前方。
cues.en: Now, if you remember, at the start of P63, we need the spacecraft sort of on its back with the rocket engine pointing out in front of them.

cues.zh: 所以计算机会请求允许这样做。
cues.en: And so the computer is asking permission to do that.

cues.zh: 如果宇航员觉得没问题，就按下“继续”键。
cues.en: If the astronauts are happy, they press the proceed key.

cues.zh: 然后计算机自动操纵飞船，让它指向正确方向。
cues.en: And then the computer automatically maneuvers the spacecraft so it's pointing the right way.

cues.zh: 计算机接下来做的是所谓的“ullage”（推进剂沉底）。
cues.en: The next thing the computer does is called allage.

cues.zh: 它会点燃部分 RCS 推力器，来一次轻微冲击。
cues.en: And it fires a little jolt through some of the RCS thrusters.

cues.zh: 这股冲劲让火箭燃料沉到燃料箱底部，好让火箭发动机第一次就能顺利点火。
cues.en: And that jolt settles the rocket fuel in the bottom of the fuel tanks, so that the rocket engine will ignite cleanly first time.

cues.zh: 所以他们真的把一切都想到了。
cues.en: So they really did think of everything.

cues.zh: 现在再把时间倒回一点。
cues.en: Now rewind the clock again.

cues.zh: 现在是点火前五秒。
cues.en: We're now five seconds before ignition.

cues.zh: 计算机闪出 Verb 99、Noun 62。
cues.en: And the computer flashes verb 99, noun 62.

cues.zh: 现在每个阿波罗宇航员都能告诉你 verb 99 noun 62 是什么意思。
cues.en: Now every Apollo astronaut can tell you what verb 99 noun 62 means.

cues.zh: 它的意思是：你确定要登月吗？
cues.en: It means, are you sure you want to land on the moon?

cues.zh: 所以宇航员有五秒钟时间冷静地伸手过去。
cues.en: So the astronauts have five seconds to calmly reach over.

cues.zh: 然后按下 proceed 键，授权计算机执行着陆。
cues.en: and press the proceed key to authorize the computer to perform the landing.

cues.zh: 好，我们都准备好了。
cues.en: So, we're all ready to go.

cues.zh: 提醒一下，我们现在呃正处于下降轨道，到了最低点，而且时间刚刚好。
cues.en: Just to remind you, we're uh in our descent orbit, we're now at the lowest point and at exactly the right time.

cues.zh: 计算机即将开始着陆机动，那我们开始吧。
cues.en: The computer is going to start the landing maneuvers, so here we go.

cues.zh: 我们知道流程，它从 P63 开始。
cues.en: Well we know how this works, it starts with P63.

cues.zh: 计算机做的第一件事，是整个软件里我最喜欢的部分。
cues.en: And the first thing the computer does is my favorite bit of the whole software.

cues.zh: 知道这一点时，我高兴坏了。
cues.en: And it made my year when I found out about it.

cues.zh: 它点燃火箭发动机。
cues.en: It lights the rocket engine.

cues.zh: 以低得可怜的 10% 推力，几乎感觉不到。
cues.en: At a very measly 10 percent thrust, so barely noticeable thrust.

cues.zh: 它会持续这样做30秒。
cues.en: And it does that for 30 seconds.

cues.zh: 那它到底在干什么呢？
cues.en: And what on earth is it doing?

cues.zh: 计算机会进行测量，看那股推力是否会让航天器旋转起来。
cues.en: Well, the computer is measuring to see whether that thrust causes the spacecraft to spin around.

cues.zh: 如果航天器开始旋转，计算机会转动火箭发动机，确保推力完全通过重心作用，这样就能止住旋转。
cues.en: And if the spacecraft starts spinning, the computer swivels the rocket engine to make sure that the the thrust acts perfectly through the center of gravity and that will stop the spinning.

cues.zh: 所以在大约30秒里，发动机轻轻地点火、火箭发动机轻轻地转动，等计算机判断没问题后，就会加大推力。
cues.en: So after about 30 seconds of sort of sort of gently firing the engine and gently swiveling the rocket engine, once the computer is happy, it ramps up the thrust.

cues.zh: 哦对，这就是我的转动。看，来了，真带劲。
cues.en: Oh yeah, there's my swiveling. There we are, it's exciting.

cues.zh: 好，现在计算机已经加大推力了。
cues.en: And there we are, so the computer has ramped up the thrust.

cues.zh: 至于为什么满推力是94%，你可以在问答环节问我。
cues.en: And for reasons you can ask me in the Q&A, full thrust is 94 percent.

cues.zh: 现在，这不是说点燃一台巨大的火箭发动机然后听天由命就行了。
cues.en: Now, this is not just a question of fire a massive rocket engine and hope for the best.

cues.zh: 整个着陆过程中，计算机一直在做复杂的制导计算，并且始终盯着两个点。
cues.en: Throughout the entire landing, the computer is running sophisticated guidance calculations and it always has two points in mind.

cues.zh: 第一个是绿色的，也就是期望着陆点。
cues.en: The first one, in green, is the desired landing site.

cues.zh: 这就是已经预先编入计算机的着陆点。
cues.en: So that's the landing site that's been programmed into the computer.

cues.zh: 而这个期望着陆点其实可以移动，我稍后会演示给你看。
cues.en: And that desired landing site can actually move, as I'll show you later.

cues.zh: 另一个是蓝色的预测着陆点。
cues.en: The other one is the projected landing site, in blue.

cues.zh: 也就是计算机根据当前位置、当前速度，通过轨道力学外推轨迹后，认为自己将要着陆的位置。
cues.en: And that's where the computer thinks it's going to land based on its current position, its current speed, and doing some orbital mechanics to extrapolate the trajectory.

cues.zh: 而计算机存在的全部意义，就是操控飞船，设法让那个预测着陆点朝期望着陆点靠拢。
cues.en: And the the computer's whole reason for existence is to steer the spacecraft to try and move that projected landing site towards the desired landing site.

cues.zh: 所以，这套东西很复杂。
cues.en: So, sophisticated stuff.

cues.zh: 好，再说一次，别管细节，就欣赏计算机大显神通吧。
cues.en: Okay, again, don't worry about the details, just enjoy the computer doing its amazing things.

cues.zh: 在 P63 阶段开始时，着陆雷达离月面太高，还无法看到月面。
cues.en: At the start of P63, the landing radar is too high above the surface to be able to to be able to see the surface.

cues.zh: 所以计算机唯一的数据来源就是 IMU。
cues.en: So the only source of data the computer has is from the IMU.

cues.zh: IMU 非常精确，但在加速飞行期间会损失精度。
cues.en: Now, the IMU is extremely accurate, but it loses accuracy during accelerated flight.

cues.zh: 当然，没有什么比屁股后面点着一台巨大的火箭发动机更能体现“加速飞行”了。
cues.en: And of course, nothing says accelerated flight like having a massive rocket engine lit up your backside.

cues.zh: 于是，计算机点亮 DSKY 上的高度灯和速度灯，告诉宇航员它并不确切知道自己在哪里，也不确切知道自己飞得多快。
cues.en: So, the computer signals to the astronauts that it doesn't know exactly where it is, or exactly how fast it's going, by illuminating the altitude and velocity lights on the disky.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 我们仍在 P63 阶段，但现在低了一些，位于月球上方 4 万英尺。此时高度已经足够低，着陆雷达能够锁定月面，并开始向制导计算机提供数据。
cues.en: We're still in P63, but we're now a bit lower, we're 40,000 feet above the moon, at which point we're low enough that the landing radar can lock onto the surface and start providing data to the guidance computer.

cues.zh: 于是当这发生时，计算机会熄灭那两盏灯，而宇航员正急切地等着这一刻。
cues.en: So when that happens, the computer clears those two lights and the astronauts are eagerly waiting for this moment.

cues.zh: 当它发生时，他们输入 Verb 6、Noun 63。
cues.en: When it happens, they type in verb 6, noun 63.

cues.zh: 意思是：请显示基于 IMU 的不准确数据你所认为的高度，与基于着陆雷达的高精度测量得到的实际高度之间的偏差。
cues.en: Which means, please show me the discrepancy between how high you thought you were based on the inaccurate data from the IMU, and how high you actually are, based on the very accurate measurement from the landing radar.

cues.zh: 在距月面 4 万英尺时，计算机认为的位置和实际位置相差 1000 英尺，这很常见。
cues.en: And it was common, 40,000 feet above the surface, for there to be a 1,000 feet discrepancy between where the computer thought it was and where it actually is.

cues.zh: 显然，当你在月球上方 4 万英尺时，一座 1000 英尺高的山丘之类并不会带来多大差别。
cues.en: Now obviously, when you're 40,000 feet above the moon, a 1,000 feet hill or there doesn't make much of a difference.

cues.zh: 但当你开始降低高度时，你真的会想开始使用更准确的数字。
cues.en: But as you start getting lower, you really want to start using the more accurate numbers.

cues.zh: 宇航员会大致检查这些数据，确认看起来还过得去；如果满意，就执行所谓的“incorporating”。
cues.en: So the astronauts kind of check this data, they sort of make sure it looks vaguely okay, and if they're happy, they do something called incorporating.

cues.zh: 要执行并入，他们输入 Verb 57，意思你猜对了：请并入；然后制导计算机会把着陆雷达提供的高精度高度信息，与 IMU 已有的信息合并，得到精确得多的位置。
cues.en: To incorporate, they type in verb 57, which means, you guessed it, please incorporate, and the guidance computer will then um merge the very accurate height information from the landing radar with the information it already has from the IMU to get a much more accurate position.

cues.zh: 随后，制导计算机会逐渐操纵飞船，修正任何偏差，因为它现在清楚自己究竟在哪里。
cues.en: And then, over time, the guidance computer will steer the spacecraft to correct for any discrepancy, now that it knows exactly where it is.

cues.zh: 好的。
cues.en: Okay.

cues.zh: 现在着陆过程已经过半。
cues.en: We're more than halfway through the landing now.

cues.zh: 在 P63 接近尾声时，计算机会在精确计算好的时刻自动逐步降低推力，让飞船保持在既定轨迹上。
cues.en: Towards the end of P63, the computer automatically ramps down the thrust at a precisely calculated time to keep the spacecraft on the trajectory.

cues.zh: 当它到达8000英尺时，会自动进入程序64。
cues.en: And then when it reaches 8,000 feet, it automatically enters program 64.

cues.zh: 那就是着陆的下一段。
cues.en: That's the next bit of the landing.

cues.zh: 嗯，从我们那两分钟的NASA训练里，就知道接下来会发生什么。
cues.en: Well, we know what happens from our 2 minutes NASA training.

cues.zh: 计算机做的第一件事，就是执行那个俯仰机动，让飞船更接近垂直姿态。
cues.en: The first thing the computer does is it does that pitch over maneuver to get the spacecraft sort of more vertical.

cues.zh: 如果还记得，在程序64期间，宇航员和计算机一起微调着陆点。
cues.en: Now, if you remember, during P64, the astronauts and the computer work together to fine tune the landing site.

cues.zh: 计算机需要某种方式，准确告诉宇航员它要在哪里着陆。
cues.en: The computer needs some way of telling the astronauts exactly where it's going to land.

cues.zh: 它需要一个非常精密的设备。
cues.en: It needs a very sophisticated device.

cues.zh: 对，就是舷窗。
cues.en: Yes, it's the window.

cues.zh: 舷窗上标着两条轴，就像这样，有点像学校里的方格纸。
cues.en: The window has these two axes marked on it, like that, a bit like graph paper in school.

cues.zh: 在程序64期间，计算机会显示Verb 6、Noun 64，意思是：我在告诉你，你将在哪里着陆。
cues.en: And during program 64, the computer shows verb 6, noun 64, and that means, I'm telling you where you're going to land.

cues.zh: 它就是这样工作的。
cues.en: And it works like this.

cues.zh: 你看到仪表盘顶行那个 5，它告诉 Armstrong 在窗口的水平轴上往左看五个刻度。
cues.en: You see that 5 on the top row of the disky, that tells Armstrong to look five along the horizontal axis in the window.

cues.zh: 右边那个 40，则告诉 Armstrong 在垂直轴上往上看 40 个刻度。
cues.en: And that 40 on the right hand side, tells Armstrong to look 40 up on the vertical axis.

cues.zh: 于是 Armstrong 就在脑中设想一个红点，正望向窗外，这个红点就是计算机在准确告诉 Armstrong，飞船究竟会降落在哪里。
cues.en: And so Armstrong then imagines a red dot looking out the window, and that red dot is the computer telling Armstrong exactly where um the spacecraft is going to land.

cues.zh: 所以在着陆的这一阶段，Buzz 会报出像 5、40 这样的数字，Armstrong 则望向窗外，用这些轴来想象那个红点，他就能看到：哦，我们要降落在那里。
cues.en: So throughout this part of the landing, Buzz will be calling out the numbers like 5, 40, and Armstrong will be looking out the window, using those axes to imagine the red dot, and he can see, oh that's where we're going to land.

cues.zh: 好，那如果 Armstrong 不满意计算机给出的着陆点呢？
cues.en: Okay, what happens if Armstrong doesn't like the look of where the computer's going to land?

cues.zh: 嗯，他可以移动手控器，而移动手控器就会改变目标着陆点。
cues.en: Well, he can move his hand controller, and if he moves his hand controller, that moves the desired landing site.

cues.zh: 然后制导算法会操纵航天器，把预计着陆点移向新的目标着陆点。
cues.en: And then the guidance algorithms will steer the spacecraft to move the projected landing site towards the new desired landing site.

cues.zh: 在 P64 整个过程中，那个假想红点在窗口里四处移动很常见，尤其是 Armstrong 用手控器改变着陆点时。
cues.en: And it was common throughout P64 for that imaginary red dot to move around the window, especially if Armstrong was using his hand controller to change the landing site.

cues.zh: 所以 Buzz 可能是在说 5、45、5、40、5、0 等等。
cues.en: So Buzz might be saying 5, 45, 5, 40, 5, 0, etcetera.

cues.zh: 而 Armstrong 一直用手控器，在需要时微调着陆点。
cues.en: And Armstrong all the time is using his hand controller to fine tune the landing site if he wants to.

cues.zh: 在整个 P64 过程中，手控器连接着呃这些非常先进的制导算法，嗯，因为手控器并不直接操纵飞船，而是移动目标着陆点。
cues.en: Throughout program 64, the hand controller is connected to uh these very sophisticated guidance algorithms, um because the the hand controller doesn't directly steer the spaceship, it moves the desired landing site.

cues.zh: 然后制导算法会算出航天器该怎么操控才能达成目标。
cues.en: And then the guidance algorithms will calculate how the spacecraft should be steered to achieve that.

cues.zh: 接着这些转向指令会下传到层级低得多的姿态控制软件，由它把转向指令转换成发给推进器的指令。
cues.en: And then those steering commands go down to the much lower level attitude control software which takes those steering commands and turns those into commands that get given to the thrusters.

cues.zh: 所以，从手控器到推进器之间隔着大量复杂的代码。
cues.en: So there's a lot of sophisticated code between the hand controller and the thrusters.

cues.zh: 一旦登月舱大致飞到着陆点上方，阿姆斯特朗就把 Pings 模式开关从自动拨到姿态保持。
cues.en: Once the lunar module is uh pretty much above the landing site, Armstrong moves that pings mode switch from auto to attitude hold.

cues.zh: 大致来说，这会让计算机自动进入程序 66。
cues.en: And roughly speaking, that automatically puts the computer into program 66.

cues.zh: 这时手控器就与复杂的制导算法断开，转而直接接入转向软件。
cues.en: At which point the hand controller is disconnected from the sophisticated guidance algorithms, and instead, is plugged directly into the steering software.

cues.zh: 也就是说，当他移动手控器时，并不是在改变着陆点，而是在直接操控航天器。
cues.en: So that means that when he moves his hand controller, rather than changing the landing site, he's directly steering the spacecraft.

cues.zh: 所以在着陆的最后阶段，这是一种更直接的控制关系。
cues.en: So it's a much more direct um relationship of control in the final stages of the landing.

cues.zh: 但我想强调的是，这并非完全手动控制。
cues.en: But the point I want to make is that it's not total manual control.

cues.zh: 始终都有代码运行在 Armstrong 的手控器和推进器之间。
cues.en: At all times, there is code running in between Armstrong's hand controller and the thrusters.

cues.zh: 最后，当登月舱非常接近地面时，会扬起大量尘土，Armstrong 再也看不清窗外。
cues.en: Finally, once the lunar module is really close to the ground, lots of dust gets kicked up and Armstrong can no longer see out the window.

cues.zh: 于是他查看座舱内的两个仪表，它们都由制导计算机控制。
cues.en: So he looks at two instruments inside the cockpit, both controlled by the guidance computer.

cues.zh: 第一个是八球仪，它告诉他航天器姿态是不是正着的。
cues.en: The first is the eight ball, and that tells him, um is the spacecraft the right way up?

cues.zh: 另一个是十字指针显示器，它告诉他是否存在横向或前后方向的速度。
cues.en: And the other one is the cross pointer display, which tells him, is there any side to side or forwards and backwards speed?

cues.zh: Armstrong 会看这两个仪表，确保飞船完全垂直，没有左右或前后的偏移。
cues.en: And Armstrong looks at these two instruments to make sure that the spacecraft is completely vertical and isn't sort of shifting side to side or forwards or backwards.

cues.zh: 这和飞行员在雾中降落飞机的做法非常相似。
cues.en: And this is very similar to how a pilot would land an aircraft in the fog.

cues.zh: 最后，你还记得飞船支脚上那些小探针吗？
cues.en: Finally, you remember those little probes on the feet of the spacecraft?

cues.zh: 一旦它们触地，座舱里就会亮起蓝色的接触指示灯。
cues.en: Well once they touch the ground, a blue contact light illuminates in the cockpit.

cues.zh: 宇航员迅速关掉发动机，松了一口气。
cues.en: The astronauts quickly switch off the engine, breathe a sigh of relief.

cues.zh: 这就是登月着陆的过程。
cues.en: And that's how you land on the moon.

cues.zh: 这就是我对阿波罗导航计算机的演示。
cues.en: And that's my demonstration of the Apollo guidance computer.

cues.zh: 不过，那些烦人的程序报警又是怎么回事呢？
cues.en: However, what about those pesky program alarms?

cues.zh: 在现代，这算是个严重问题。
cues.en: Well, in modern day like that's a serious problem.

cues.zh: 这有点像在电脑上看到那个提示，或者如果你更老派一点，看到的是这样的东西。
cues.en: That's a bit like seeing that on your computer, or if you're a if you're a little bit more more old school, something like that.

cues.zh: 或者最糟糕的是，居然会那样！
cues.en: Or worst of all, that!

cues.zh: 如果你就在飞船里，1202 警报可没什么好笑的。
cues.en: The 1202 alarm was nothing to laugh about if you're in the spaceship itself.

cues.zh: 当然，他们一直都有中止任务这个选项。
cues.en: Now, of course, they always had the option of aborting.

cues.zh: 但中止任务绝不是件小事。
cues.en: But an abort was by no means a trivial thing.

cues.zh: 显然，你会损失掉已经花在这项任务上的数十亿美元，至少也是数亿美元。
cues.en: Obviously, you lose billions of dollars that have been spent on the, or at least hundreds of millions, on the mission.

cues.zh: 你会失去大量的国家自豪感，还有你自己的自尊。
cues.en: You lose a huge amount of national pride and your own pride.

cues.zh: 但撇开这些不谈，中止任务在技术上其实非常困难。
cues.en: But aside from all of that, it's actually technically very difficult to abort.

cues.zh: 所以如果他们按下中止按钮，四个火工螺栓就会爆炸。
cues.en: So if they pushed the abort button, four pyrotechnic bolts would have exploded.

cues.zh: 它们会把登月舱分成两半，整个下降级会脱离，只留下上升级。
cues.en: They would have separated the lunar module into two, so the whole descent stage would have come away, just leaving the ascent stage.

cues.zh: 第五个火工装置会被触发，它会让一把铡刀切断连接两级的所有线缆。
cues.en: A fifth pyrotechnic would have fired, which would have fired a guillotine across all of the cables connecting the two stages together.

cues.zh: 这样就彻底把飞船分成了两部分。
cues.en: So completely separating the spacecraft in two.

cues.zh: 所以，呃，你大概只能中止一次，你懂我意思吧，没法再来一次。
cues.en: So, uh you sort of you can only abort once, if you know what I mean, you can't have another go.

cues.zh: 然后当然，嗯，指令舱里的 Mike Collins 要解决一个很大的轨道力学问题，因为他得去接他的同伴。
cues.en: And then of course, um Mike Collins in the command module has a very big orbital mechanics problem to solve because he has to go and pick up his friends.

cues.zh: 所以中止是一件完全不简单、也不安全的事。
cues.en: So an abort was a completely non-trivial and not safe thing to do.

cues.zh: 所以，如何处理 1202 警报是一个非常严肃的问题。
cues.en: So the question of what we do about the 1202 alarm was a very serious one.

cues.zh: 所以这就是我想在演讲后半部分讲的内容。
cues.en: And so that's what I'd like to talk about in the latter half of the presentation.

cues.zh: 首先，我想简单讲讲任务软件。
cues.en: So first, I want to talk a bit about the mission software.

cues.zh: 然后我们会再回到驾驶舱，弄清那些程序警报的根源。
cues.en: And then we'll leak back into the cockpit and get to the bottom of those program alarms.

cues.zh: 不过首先，先简单说说软件。
cues.en: First though, a little bit about the software.

cues.zh: 接下来这10分钟会稍微枯燥一点，但请耐心听我讲完。
cues.en: Now, this is a a sort of a a slightly uh drier 10 minutes of the talk, but just bear with me, let me say what I've got to say.

cues.zh: 然后我们会回到飞船里，在最后15分钟好好玩一玩。
cues.en: Uh and then we'll we'll jump back into the spaceship and have fun for the last 15 minutes.

cues.zh: 登月舱里的软件叫 Luminary。
cues.en: The software in the lunar module was called Luminary.

cues.zh: 希望我的演示能让你相信，这是一套精密的设备。
cues.en: And I hope in my demo I've persuaded you it was a sophisticated piece of kit.

cues.zh: 它控制着整个任务的各个阶段。
cues.en: It controlled all phases of the mission.

cues.zh: 它把登月舱送入了那条椭圆下降轨道。
cues.en: So it got the lunar module into that elliptical descent orbit.

cues.zh: 它负责整个着陆过程，就是我刚才讲的那些。
cues.en: It managed all of the landing, that's the stuff I've just been talking about.

cues.zh: 它把你带离月球，再让你与指令舱会合。
cues.en: It got you off the moon again and it got you rendezvoused back with the command module.

cues.zh: 所以它什么都干了。
cues.en: So it did everything.

cues.zh: 如我们所见，它控制着那台巨大的火箭发动机，还点火了 RCS 推进器。
cues.en: And as we've seen, it controlled that massive rocket engine, it fired the RCS thrusters.

cues.zh: 它在更新 DSKY 上的信息，在移动八球和十字指针显示。
cues.en: It was updating information on the disky, it was moving the eight ball and the cross pointer display.

cues.zh: 从 IMU 和着陆雷达读取数据，同时做各种事情。
cues.en: Reading data from the IMU and the landing radar, doing all sorts of things all at the same time.

cues.zh: 所以它运行的是一个非常简单的实时操作系统，是他们作为 Luminary 的一部分从零编写的。
cues.en: So it ran a very simple real-time operating system that they wrote from scratch as part of Luminary.

cues.zh: 我想很快讲讲他们在这个实时操作系统中用来保证可靠性的六条设计原则。
cues.en: And I want to very quickly talk about six design principles that they used in that real-time operating system to make it reliable.

cues.zh: 哦，我总忘了提这一点，Luminary 的源码在 GitHub 上可以找到。对，很好。
cues.en: Oh, I always forget this bit, the source for Luminary is available on GitHub. Yes, very good.

cues.zh: 好，第一条。
cues.en: Okay, number one.

cues.zh: 使用高级语言。
cues.en: Use a high level language.

cues.zh: 正如我一开始说的，阿波罗制导计算机的指令非常原始，很难使用。
cues.en: So as I said towards the start, the Apollo guidance computer's instructions were very primitive and difficult to use.

cues.zh: 这就意味着，面对这些复杂的制导算法，很难把它们翻译成正确的代码。
cues.en: And that meant that you had these complicated guidance algorithms and it was difficult to translate those into code that was correct.

cues.zh: 而且，15 位整数——也就是计算机能存的小数值——不足以提供制导计算机所需的那种精度。
cues.en: Also, the 15 bit integers, the the small numbers that the computer can store, were not big enough to give the kind of accurate precision that the guidance computer needed.

cues.zh: 所以他们的解决办法是一种叫“解释器”的东西。
cues.en: So their solution to this was something called the interpreter.

cues.zh: 它提供了一套虚拟指令，功能要强大得多。
cues.en: This provided a sort of virtual set of instructions that were much more powerful.

cues.zh: 比如，它提供了矩阵和向量运算，做制导计算时非常有用。
cues.en: So for example, they gave you matrix and vector operations which are really useful if you're doing guidance calculations.

cues.zh: 它还提供了些“奢侈”功能，比如能按索引访问数组；也提供了栈，很适合写更有结构、更易读的代码。
cues.en: They gave you such luxuries as being able to index into an array and they gave you a stack which is good for writing um much more structured readable code.

cues.zh: 它绕过了 15 位字长的限制，提供双精度和三精度整数，因此能处理的数字大得多。
cues.en: It got round the 15 bit word size by giving you double and triple precision integers, so it gave you much bigger numbers to work with.

cues.zh: 这让你在这些计算中获得了真正需要的精度，嗯，比如确定着陆点、以及该怎么操控航天器等等。
cues.en: And that gave you the accuracy that you really needed for those calculations, uh you know, working out the landing site and how you should steer the spacecraft, etcetera.

cues.zh: 这还意味着同一个算法占用的空间小得多，因为每条指令都能替你完成更多事情。
cues.en: It also meant that the same algorithm took up a lot less space because each instruction did a lot more things for you.

cues.zh: 所以完成任务所需的指令也更少。
cues.en: So you needed fewer of them to get the job done.

cues.zh: 如果你还记得，当时内存非常少，所以程序占用空间更小是件大好事。
cues.en: And if you remember, there wasn't very much memory, so if your program took up less space, that was a really good thing.

cues.zh: 这也让写出正确的代码更容易，因为指令更好用；但解释器的缺点是运行得非常慢。
cues.en: It also made it easier to write correct code because the instructions were easier to use, but the downside of the interpreter was it ran really slowly.

cues.zh: 所以最终的软件是两者的结合：真正对时间要求很高的部分，比如控制推进器或读取 IMU 数据，必须一直进行，而且要及时完成。
cues.en: So the final software was a blend of both things, the really time critical stuff like controlling the thrusters or reading data from the IMU that had to be done all the time and in a really timely manner.

cues.zh: 这些代码是用难以使用的低级语言写成的，解释器本身也必须用这种难以使用的语言来写。
cues.en: Those were written in the difficult to use low level language, and the interpreter itself had to be written in the difficult to use language as well.

cues.zh: 但后来那些做复杂数学运算的高级制导算法，都被写进了这个解释器里。
cues.en: But then all of this deluxe guidance algorithms that were doing complicated maths, were written in the interpreter.

cues.zh: 它们之所以能做到这一点，是因为这些制导算法只需要每秒或每三秒重新计算一次。
cues.en: And they could do that because those guidance algorithms only had to recalculate stuff every second or every three seconds.

cues.zh: 所以即使运行得慢也没关系。
cues.en: So it didn't matter if they ran slowly.

cues.zh: 第二点。
cues.en: Number two.

cues.zh: 把你的系统拆分成一个个作业。
cues.en: Divide your system into jobs.

cues.zh: 制导计算机同时在处理很多事情。
cues.en: The guidance computer was doing lots of things, sort of all at the same time.

cues.zh: 于是他们把系统拆成一个个作业，每个作业只做一件事，有点像你手机上的不同应用。
cues.en: And so they split the system up into jobs where each job did one thing, a bit like different apps on your phone.

cues.zh: 比如有个作业叫 Redax，它从 IMU 读取数据，再用这些数据计算航天器的位置和速度。
cues.en: So for example, there was a job called Redax, which read data from the IMU and used that to calculate the position and the speed of the spacecraft.

cues.zh: 有一整套作业，用来实现数字自动驾驶仪。
cues.en: There was a whole suite of jobs used to implement the digital autopilot.

cues.zh: 有个名字很可爱的作业叫 pinball，pinball 负责更新 DSKY 上的数字。
cues.en: There was a charmingly named job called pinball, and pinball updated the numbers on the disky.

cues.zh: 有些作业负责高层任务，比如 P63、P64 等等，还有呃几十个我没列在这里的其他作业。
cues.en: There were jobs for the high level tasks like P63, P64 etcetera, and um tens of other jobs that I haven't even included here.

cues.zh: 如果只记住一件事，请记住：每个作业都有一小块可以使用的内存。
cues.en: If you remember one thing, remember this, each job had a small area of memory that it could use.

cues.zh: 算是临时存储，有点像它做计算时，有一块空间能展示自己的运算过程。
cues.en: For sort of temporary storage, a bit like if it was doing some calculations, it had some space where it could sort of show it's working.

cues.zh: 内存足够让七个作业同时运行。
cues.en: And there was enough memory to have seven jobs on the go at any one time.

cues.zh: 他们非常仔细、极其仔细地设计了系统，确保同时运行的作业永远不会超过七个。
cues.en: And they very carefully, really carefully designed the system so you would never have more than seven jobs running at the same time.

cues.zh: 第三点。
cues.en: Number three.

cues.zh: 失败时重启。
cues.en: Restart on failure.

cues.zh: 作为一名头发花白的软件工程师，我得说，所有软件都会遇到故障，这是残酷的现实。
cues.en: Now, speaking as a grey haired software engineer, it is a sad fact of life that all software will encounter failures.

cues.zh: 我指的不是程序员误解了程序该做什么，或者程序员偷懒导致的 bug。
cues.en: Now I'm not talking about bugs where the programmer misunderstood what the program should do, or the programmer was lazy.

cues.zh: 那些问题在测试阶段早就该被发现了。
cues.en: Those things would be caught much earlier during testing.

cues.zh: 我说的是百万分之一、极其罕见的事件。
cues.en: I'm talking about one in a million, once in a blue moon kind of events that are really rare.

cues.zh: 而这些极其罕见的事件，可能触发软件中不寻常的代码路径，如果你没考虑到那种可能性，就可能导致软件失败。
cues.en: And those really rare events can trigger unusual code flows through the software that can cause the software to fail if you sort of didn't think about that eventuality.

cues.zh: 而且你在测试中通常也发现不了这些问题，因为它们百万次才发生一次。
cues.en: And you often wouldn't wouldn't find these things during testing because they only happen one in a million times.

cues.zh: 所以测试时你得非常走运，才能触发这个错误条件。
cues.en: So you'd have to be really lucky during testing to hit the error condition.

cues.zh: 软件一旦失效，就不能指望它自己恢复。
cues.en: If your software has failed, it cannot be trusted to recover itself.

cues.zh: 它已经失效了，那就什么都说不准了。
cues.en: It's failed, so all bets are off.

cues.zh: 所以换个办法，重启出故障的那部分软件。
cues.en: So instead, you restart the bit of software that's failed.

cues.zh: 希望在于，重启软件后，导致它故障的瞬态条件已经消失，软件可以再试一次，希望这次能正常工作，系统也随之恢复。
cues.en: And the hope is that if you restart the software, whatever transient condition was happening that caused it to fail, will have gone away, the software can have another go, and hopefully this time it will work, and the system will recover.

cues.zh: 制导计算机提供了几级重启，你可以只重启失败的作业，也可以重启一组作业。
cues.en: The guidance computer provided several levels of restart, so you could restart just the failed job, you could restart a group of jobs.

cues.zh: 你也可以重启一切，但保留关键信息，比如你当前的位置和着陆点，不受影响。
cues.en: You could restart everything, but leave vital information, like where you are and where you're landing, intact.

cues.zh: 那叫做 PODO。
cues.en: That was called a PODO.

cues.zh: 你也可以在 Q&A 环节问我这个。
cues.en: You can you can ask me about that in the Q&A as well.

cues.zh: 嗯，或者你可以直接把硬件关掉再重新打开，那叫做全新启动。
cues.en: Um, or you could literally switch the hardware off and back on again, that was called a fresh start.

cues.zh: 好了，我们进行到一半了，请耐心听我讲这些设计原则。
cues.en: Okay, we're halfway through, so bear with me on the design principles.

cues.zh: 第四点，为你的良好状态设置检查点。
cues.en: Number four, checkpoint your good state.

cues.zh: 重启很好，但你会丢失任务当时正在做的一切。
cues.en: So restarting is great, but you lose whatever it was that your job was doing.

cues.zh: 所以，当任务到达一个合适的点，也就是检查点，它可以把这个点保存下来供以后使用。
cues.en: So, when your job reaches a sensible point called a checkpoint, it can save that point for later.

cues.zh: 然后，如果任务被重启，它可以读入已保存的内容，并从上次中断的地方继续。
cues.en: And then, if the job gets restarted, it can read in what it saved and pick up from where it left off.

cues.zh: 例如，如果你的任务是从 IMU 读取大量数据，最终计算位置和速度。
cues.en: For example, if you're the job that reads loads of data from the IMU, and then eventually calculates the position and the speed.

cues.zh: 你会做大量计算，最终得到一个结果。
cues.en: You'll be doing lots of of calculations, and then eventually you'll get a result.

cues.zh: 所以，一旦得到合理的结果，你可能会设置检查点；这样作业重启时，就能读入上次计算到的位置，并从那里继续。
cues.en: And so, once you have a sensible result, you might checkpoint that so that if your job gets restarted, you can read in the position that you last calculated and pick up from there.

cues.zh: 你可能会问，如果检查点坏了怎么办；这种情况下，像 PODO 和全新启动这类更激进的重启方式，会清除检查点。
cues.en: You might say, what happens if the checkpoint is bad and the, in that case the more draconian restarts like the PODO and the fresh start, would clear out the checkpoint.

cues.zh: 这样作业就得多做些工作才能恢复运行，但至少是从空白状态开始。
cues.en: So jobs would have to sort of do more work to get back up and running, but they would at least be starting from a a blank slate.

cues.zh: 还有谁吗？很好。那么，我想再次感谢 Robert 带来这场非常精彩的演讲。也非常感谢大家到场。能跟一群看起来有兴趣的人聊我真正感兴趣的话题，真的很开心，特别有意思。我在很多阿波罗影片里见过窗户上的网格线，一直好奇：头部位置肯定有影响，他们是怎么处理的？嗯，窗户是双层或三层玻璃，其中两块玻璃上各有一个十字；阿姆斯特朗会确保自己向外看时，让两个十字重合。
cues.en: Any anyone else? Excellent. Well uh, once again, I'd like to uh thank uh Robert for an absolutely fascinating talk. Um and could I say thank you very much for coming? It's a real pleasure to be able to talk about something that I'm really interested in, to a group of people who look interested. It's absolutely fun. I've seen the graticules on the window in in lots of uh Apollo films, and what I've always wondered is surely it matters where your head is and how did they manage that? Um so the window was either double or triple glazed, and on two of the panels was a a cross, so Armstrong would make sure that he was looking out so that the two crosses merged together.

cues.zh: 而且，这在如今的飞机驾驶舱里也很常见。
cues.en: And again, that's that's common in aircraft cockpits today as well.

cues.zh: 呃，阿波罗计划始于 60 年代初。我想问，这个计算机系统——您刚才重点讲了很多下降阶段——但从阿波罗 1 号到阿波罗 10 号，他们只是尝试飞往月球，还没有着陆，这个计算机系统当时处于什么开发阶段？在阿波罗 1 号到 10 号中，如果它发挥了作用，又扮演了什么角色？
cues.en: Uh the Apollo program started in the early 60s, and I'm wondering this computer system, you've you've focused a lot on the descent, but from Apollo 1 to Apollo 10, where they were just attempting to travel to the moon, but not not land, what stage was this computer system developed and what part did it play if any, in the in Apollo 1 to 10?

cues.zh: 嗯，这个我没有确切答案。
cues.en: Um, I don't have a precise answer to that.

cues.zh: 所以有一件事这台计算机没做，就是把你送离地球。
cues.en: So the one thing the computer didn't do was getting you off the earth.

cues.zh: Saturn V 火箭里有一台单独的计算机负责这件事。
cues.en: There was a separate computer in the Saturn V rocket that did that.

cues.zh: 所以像早期“先离开地球”这类事情，他们并不需要这台计算机。
cues.en: So the kind of very early stuff of let's just get off the earth, they didn't need this computer for.

cues.zh: 这台计算机大概有两个主要的迭代版本，Block 1 和 Block 2。
cues.en: There were two sort of major uh major iterations of this computer, block one and block two.

cues.zh: Block Two 是把人送上月球的计算机，Block One 则是更原始的机器。
cues.en: Block two was the computer that got you to the moon, block one was a more primitive machine.

cues.zh: 我猜早期的一些阿波罗任务中用过一些 Block One，可能是 Apollo 8。
cues.en: I suspect that they flew some block ones during some of the early Apollos, possibly Apollo 8.

cues.zh: 嗯，但他们遇到的问题之一是软件需求不断变得更复杂，所以他们在 63 或 64 年意识到 Block One 机器不够用了，因此不得不为 Block Two 重做很多东西。嗯，所以它确实执行过一些早期任务，但我不确定具体是哪些。还有其他问题吗？
cues.en: Um, but one of the problems they had was that the requirements of the software kept getting more complex, and so they realized in 63 or 4 that the block one machine wasn't going to cut it, and so they had to redo a lot of things for the block two. Um, so it did fly some of the early missions, but I don't know exactly which. Any other questions?

cues.zh: 我只是想知道，在开发期间，MIT 那边的人有没有这个的软件仿真之类的东西，还是他们直接在硬件上工作？
cues.en: I'm just wondering during development, did they have a software emulation or something of this back on the MIT people, or were they working on hardware?

cues.zh: 他们两者都有。
cues.en: They they had both.

cues.zh: 不过按理说那真的相当困难，因为正如你所说，硬件与输入输出紧密绑定，实时行为肯定也非常不同吧？
cues.en: And but presumably that was really quite difficult because, as you said, the hardware is so intimately tied to the inputs and outputs and the real time behavior must have been very different?

cues.zh: 是的。
cues.en: Yes.

cues.zh: 嗯。我……我可以再多说一些。我不确定你还有没有别的问题。
cues.en: Um. To to, I can, I can say more. I wasn't sure if you had any more questions.

cues.zh: 我想说的是，这能说明我们今天做事方式上的什么吗？
cues.en: I was going to say, is that going to tell you anything about how we do things today?

cues.zh: 所以，嗯，这台计算机很棒的一点是，有几十万页的文档、测试日志以及各种东西。
cues.en: So, um, one of the lovely things about this computer is there are hundreds of thousands of pages of documentation and test logs and all sorts of things.

cues.zh: 所以它真是个宝库。
cues.en: So it's a real treasure trove.

cues.zh: 我发现其中一件事是，有海量页面，嗯，都是做仿真的结果。
cues.en: One of the things I found, a huge numbers of pages of um the results of doing simulations.

cues.zh: 所以他们会仿真计算机执行登月任务。
cues.en: So they would simulate running the computer landing on the moon.

cues.zh: 所以他们显然有能力以精密的方式仿真 IMU 之类的东西，来测试软件。
cues.en: So they they clearly had the capability to simulate things like the IMU um in a sophisticated way to test the software.

cues.zh: 嗯，我愿付出一切代价，只求得到一份那个仿真软件；但据我所知，到目前为止还没人找到它。不过我的理解是，他们确实做过极其复杂的仿真。
cues.en: Um I would I would give my right arm for a copy of that simulation software, but so far to my knowledge, no one's found it, but my understanding is they did do extremely sophisticated simulations.

cues.zh: 你另一个问题是：这和今天有什么关系？
cues.en: And your other question was how does that tie into today?

cues.zh: 所以，比如说，我们以前也做过类似的系统——是的，是的，我们做过——嗯，对，我们会运行软件仿真和硬件仿真。
cues.en: So, for example, we used to do something similar to the systems where, yes, yes, we do, um, we yeah, we would run software simulations and hardware simulations.

cues.zh: 嗯，对。
cues.en: Um, yeah.

cues.zh: 我想说，他们对那个软件所做的测试水平，和今天你对比如飞机软件所做的测试相当，它确实测试得非常充分。
cues.en: I would say that the the level of testing that they did for the software is comparable to the testing you would do for say, an airplane software today, like it was very well tested.

cues.zh: 太好了。
cues.en: Great.

cues.zh: 还有谁要问吗？没有了？太好了。
cues.en: Any anyone else, or we Excellent.
